notes.text:
HISTORY AND PHYSICAL. Chart, labs and overnight events reviewed. 61-year-old male admitted for upper GI bleed. Admission data:
Day 0: labs bilirubin 0.8, creatinine 1.08, hemoglobin 14.9, platelets 226, sodium 140, wbc 8.1; vitals dbp 65-68, heart_rate 81-85, map 87-91, o2_flow 0, resp_rate 14-16, sbp 132-138, spo2 96-98, temp 36.6-36.8
Day 0 orders/meds/results: EGD: mild nonbleeding gastritis; Pantoprazole 80 mg IV
Assessment and plan: Upper GI bleed. Hypertension. Acute blood loss anemia.

PROGRESS NOTE, hospital day 1. Patient seen and examined at bedside. Data:
Day 1: labs creatinine 1.1, hemoglobin 14.8, platelets 224, sodium 140, wbc 7.4; vitals dbp 64-69, heart_rate 81-86, map 89-91, o2_flow 0, resp_rate 15-16, sbp 131-138, spo2 97-98, temp 36.6-36.8
Assessment and plan: Upper GI bleed. Hypertension. Acute blood loss anemia. Continue current management.

DISCHARGE SUMMARY. 61-year-old male, length of stay 2 days. Hospital course: treated per the plan above with daily labs and vital signs; stable for discharge. Medications reconciled and return precautions reviewed. Discharge diagnoses: Upper GI bleed. Hypertension. Acute blood loss anemia. Follow up with primary care in one week. Patient seen and examined at bedside.
